---
title: "Architecture"
---

The backend is built on [Django](https://www.djangoproject.com/) + [Django REST Framework](https://www.django-rest-framework.org/), with [Celery](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/) for asynchronous tasks and [Postgres/PostGIS](https://postgis.net/) for data storage. The frontend is served via [R Shiny](https://shiny.rstudio.com/). The backend exposes a RESTful API consumed by the R Shiny frontend, handling all business logic including geometry validation, chemistry data lookup, report creation, and asynchronous report generation.

The system is containerized using [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) and orchestrated with [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/), allowing for easy deployment and scalability.

## Overview

The system is composed of:

- **API Layer**
  REST endpoints for geometry operations, chemistry queries, report creation, and downloading generated reports.

- **Database Layer**
  PostgreSQL with PostGIS enabled.
  Stores:
  - User accounts
  - Reports
  - Report grid payloads (JSON)
  - Chemistry results
  - Dataset versioning metadata

- **Task Layer (Celery)**
  Used for:
  - Running spatial operations
  - Generating PDF reports
  - Heavy GIS or data-processing tasks

- **Static + Reverse Proxy Layer**
  Caddy serves:
  - The R Shiny frontend
  - Django API backend
  - Static assets
  - Internal documentation

- **Frontend Layer**
  R Shiny application providing the GUI for users to interact with the system.

## Data Flow

1. Client interacts with the R Shiny frontend.
2. Frontend makes REST API calls to the Django backend for operations.
3. Backend processes requests, performing spatial operations and data lookups as needed.
4. For long-running tasks (e.g., report generation), backend enqueues tasks in Celery.
5. Celery workers process tasks asynchronously, updating the database with results.
6. Frontend retrieves results from the backend and displays them to the user.
